questions.question: In a layered library structure, which dependency should be forbidden?
options: A feature library importing a ui library
A ui library importing a data-access library that calls HttpClient
A data-access library importing a util library
A feature library importing a util library
questions.explanation: UI libraries should stay presentational; letting them depend on data-access couples visual components to APIs and state.

questions.question: What is the main reason to adopt micro frontends?
options: They always make the app load faster
They remove the need for shared dependencies
They let teams that cannot coordinate releases build and deploy independently
They are required for lazy loading in Angular
questions.explanation: Micro frontends solve an organisational problem (independent deployment) and add runtime costs such as shared-version skew.

questions.question: How do you send every uncaught Angular error to a telemetry service?
options: Provide a custom class for the ErrorHandler token
questions.explanation: Angular routes uncaught errors to ErrorHandler; providing your own implementation centralises reporting.

questions.question: What does the `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` ESLint rule do?
options: Splits the bundle into lazy chunks
Generates index.ts files for each library
Fails linting when an import crosses a dependency constraint defined by project tags
questions.explanation: It checks imports against depConstraints (for example type:ui may only depend on type:ui and type:util) and reports violations as lint errors.
